country.name: South Korea
country.tagline: Campbell Early and wild meoru grapes in the 'wine county' of Yeongdong.

stats.note: Small production, mostly from American and native grapes.

country.overview:
Korea's traditional drinks are rice-based, but grapes grow widely, and a small wine industry uses mostly Campbell Early, an American table grape, plus Muscat Bailey A and the native wild grape meoru (Vitis coignetiae). Majuang, launched by Oriental Brewing in 1977, was the first well-known Korean grape wine. Today the centre is Yeongdong County in North Chungcheong, which promotes itself as Korea's wine county, with dozens of small farm wineries and the company Wine Korea; the island of Daebudo, near Ansan, is another Campbell Early area. Monsoon summers and cold winters make vinifera difficult.

Korean winemakers face a short, wet summer monsoon and cold winters, so most vineyards use hardy American or hybrid grapes rather than vinifera. Campbell Early and meoru give sweet or off-dry wines with a grapey, foxy character, and producers also make wines from fruits such as Korean black raspberry (bokbunja). Yeongdong's farm wineries and grape festival draw visitors, and a small number of growers are experimenting with Muscat Bailey A and cold-hardy hybrids. Most wine drunk in Korea is imported.

history.title: Majuang
history.text: Oriental Brewing launched Majuang, the first widely sold Korean grape wine.

history.title: Yeongdong farm wineries
history.text: Yeongdong County supported grape growers to open small farm wineries, becoming the centre of Korean wine.

country.climate_soils: Continental monsoon climate: hot, wet summers and cold winters.

grapes.name: Campbell Early
grapes.note: The dominant grape, American in origin, used for table and wine.

grapes.name: Meoru (Vitis coignetiae)
grapes.note: Native wild grape used for distinctive dark wines.

sites.name: Yeongdong wine county
sites.text: Yeongdong County in North Chungcheong grows much of Korea's Campbell Early grapes and has encouraged farmers to make wine; it hosts a grape and wine festival and dozens of small farm wineries.

sites.name: Daebudo
sites.text: An island linked to the mainland by a sea wall near Ansan, west of Seoul, where Campbell Early grapes grown in sea breezes supply local wineries.
